title: alert first word is type
rule: First word is the type: Informative / Warning / Success / Error / Emergency (or a more precise first word such as “Announcement”). Heading ≤1 line. Extra detail in the body, not a second heading line. Users must not rely on colour or icon alone.
pass_when: Heading starts with the type (or a more precise first word), stays on one line, and meaning is not colour/icon-only.
fail_when: Type is only an icon/colour; heading wraps to a second line of detail.
overview: Alert headings start with the type word and stay on one line without color-only meaning.
apply_when: Writing USWDS alert headings for informative, warning, success, error, or emergency.
not_when: Toasts or inline field errors that use different heading patterns.
agent_hint: Start the alert heading with the type; keep one line; never rely on color or icon alone.
description: USWDS alert headings begin with the type—Informative, Warning, Success, Error, Emergency, or a more precise first word such as “Announcement”—and stay on one line. Extra detail goes in the body, not a second heading line. Users must not rely on colour or icon alone. Type shown only as icon/colour, or a heading that wraps into detail, fails the pattern.
